say.en: Look behind your lab computers: cables with clear plastic plugs, a box with blinking lights, and somewhere a router. Each piece has a specific job. In this lesson: State the function of modem, NIC, RJ45, repeater, hub, switch, router and gateway.

body.en: A *modem* (modulator–demodulator) converts digital data to analog signals for transmission over telephone or cable lines and back. An Ethernet card or Network Interface Card (NIC) connects a computer to a network; it has the MAC address. RJ45 is an eight-pin jack used to connect Ethernet cables. A repeater regenerates weakened signals, since a signal on an Ethernet cable weakens after about 100 m.

narration.en: A modem converts between digital and analog, the NIC connects a computer to the network, RJ45 is the cable plug, and a repeater boosts weak signals.
narration.kn: ಮೋಡೆಮ್ ಡಿಜಿಟಲ್–ಅನಲಾಗ್ ಪರಿವರ್ತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, NIC ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರನ್ನು ಜಾಲಕ್ಕೆ ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, RJ45 ಕೇಬಲ್ ಪ್ಲಗ್, ರಿಪೀಟರ್ ದುರ್ಬಲ ಸಂಕೇತವನ್ನು ಪುನರುತ್ಪಾದಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: PC A sends a frame to one computer. A hub repeats every frame to all its ports, so every computer receives it and the others must drop it. A switch learns which MAC address is on which port and forwards the frame only there. Send to C through the hub, then through the switch. How many copies travel each time? Why does a switch make a busy network faster and more private?

title.en: On the board: A home network and its devices

say.en: Each computer has a network interface card with its own MAC address. An Ethernet cable plugs in with an RJ45 jack.
A switch joins the computers of a LAN. It sends each frame only to the destination port, using MAC addresses. A hub would send it to every port.
A router connects different networks and forwards packets using IP addresses.
A modem converts digital data to signals for the telephone or cable line, and back. A gateway is the network’s entry and exit, often with a firewall.
On a long cable the signal weakens after about 100 metres; a repeater regenerates it.

body.en: A hub connects several computers and sends incoming data to all ports, which wastes bandwidth and causes collisions. A *switch* also connects computers but forwards data only to the destination port, using MAC addresses. A router connects different networks and forwards packets towards their destination using IP addresses. A gateway is the entry and exit point of a network, connecting it to outside networks that may use different protocols; it often also acts as a firewall.

narration.en: A hub broadcasts to everyone, a switch sends only to the right computer, a router connects different networks, and a gateway is the door to the outside world.
narration.kn: ಹಬ್ ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಸ್ವಿಚ್ ಸರಿಯಾದ ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್‌ಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ, ರೂಟರ್ ಬೇರೆ ಜಾಲಗಳನ್ನು ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಗೇಟ್‌ವೇ ಹೊರಜಗತ್ತಿಗೆ ಬಾಗಿಲು.

myth.en: A hub and a switch are the same: both connect computers, so it does not matter which I choose.

truth.en: A hub broadcasts every message to all connected devices, wasting bandwidth and causing collisions. A switch learns which device is on which port and sends each message only to its destination, so it is faster and more secure. They look alike and both sit in the middle of a star network. The difference is inside: broadcast versus targeted delivery.

say.en: Modem converts digital ↔ analogue; NIC connects a computer; RJ45 is the cable plug.
Repeater regenerates weak signals; hub broadcasts; switch delivers to one port.
Router joins networks using IP addresses; gateway joins networks with different protocols.
PAN < LAN < MAN < WAN by area; the Internet is the largest WAN.
Bus (backbone), star (central switch), tree (stars on a backbone), ring (loop), mesh (all to all, n(n−1)/2 links).

problem.en: A small office has 12 computers and a broadband line. List the devices needed to connect them and the Internet, with the job of each.

steps.en: A NIC in each computer, with Ethernet cables ending in RJ45 connectors.
A 16-port switch to connect the 12 computers into a LAN.
A modem to convert signals on the broadband line.
A router (often combined with the modem) to connect the office LAN to the ISP's network.

answer.en: NICs + RJ45 cables, a switch, a modem and a router.
